name: El Salvador
summary: Blue, white and blue horizontal bands with the coat of arms in the centre: a triangle containing five volcanoes, a Phrygian cap and a rainbow, inside a wreath and the words 'República de El Salvador en la América Central'.
origin: El Salvador used the blue and white of the Federal Republic of Central America after independence. Between 1865 and 1912 it used a flag modelled on the US flag, with stars on a red canton.
On 27 May 1912 it returned to the blue-white-blue Central American design, with a new coat of arms.

colors.name: Blue
colors.meaning: The two oceans, the Pacific and the Caribbean (Atlantic), that border Central America.

colors.name: White
colors.meaning: Peace and the land between the oceans.

symbols.name: Triangle with volcanoes
symbols.description: An equilateral triangle with five volcanoes rising from the sea.
symbols.meaning: Equality; the five volcanoes are the five members of the former Federal Republic of Central America.

symbols.name: Phrygian cap and rainbow
symbols.description: A red liberty cap on a staff, under a rainbow.

history.label: US-style flag
history.note: Blue and white stripes with stars on a red canton.

facts: Nicaragua's flag is very similar, with a different emblem showing the same five volcanoes.
Its unusual 189:335 ratio is set by law.
Honduras's flag uses the same blue-white-blue with five stars instead of volcanoes.
clues: Blue, white and blue bands with a triangular emblem of five volcanoes and a liberty cap.
Its emblem's text names its country 'in Central America'.
From 1865 to 1912 it used a flag copied from the US.
